Mean and variance of the log-rank statistic over calendar time

Source: R/lr_moments.R
lr_moments.Rd

Computes, at each calendar time, the expected events, the mean of the log-rank score U (observed minus expected events in the treatment group), its information V (the limit of the usual variance estimator) and the mean and variance of the standardized statistic Z = -U / sqrt(V), which is positive when the treatment is better.

Usage

lr_moments(
  scenario,
  n,
  calendar_time,
  endpoint = c("os", "pfs"),
  mean = c("direct", "schoenfeld"),
  variance = c("null", "alternative", "studentized"),
  trigger = NULL
)

Arguments

scenario

An ms_scenario object.

n

Total sample size.

calendar_time

Calendar times (positive).

endpoint

"os" or "pfs".

mean

"direct" or "schoenfeld".

variance

"null", "alternative" or "studentized".

trigger

Endpoint whose observed number of events determines each calendar time ("os" or "pfs"; one value or one per time), or NULL or NA for fixed calendar times. Used only with variance = "studentized".

Value

A data frame with time, events_control, events_treatment, events, score_mean, info, z_mean and z_var.

Details

Let y0 and y1 be the probabilities of being at risk at follow-up time s in each group, multiplied by the allocation probabilities and by the enrolled fraction at t - s. Then E(U) = n times the integral of y0 y1 / (y0 + y1) (lambda1 - lambda0) and V = n times the integral of y0 y1 / (y0 + y1)^2 (y0 lambda0 + y1 lambda1), from 0 to t.

The mean of Z is

  • mean = "direct": -E(U) / sqrt(V), the mean of Yung and Liu (2020, Section 2.3.3);

  • mean = "schoenfeld": -sqrt(p0 p1 D) times the event-weighted average of the log hazard ratio, where D is the expected number of events (Schoenfeld 1981).

The variance of Z is 1 for variance = "null". For variance = "alternative" it is the asymptotic variance of the score under the alternative divided by V, from Luo et al. (2019), which accounts for the variability of the numbers at risk. This variance assumes simple randomization; Yung and Liu (2020) show that block randomization gives a variance that is not larger. For variance = "studentized" it is the asymptotic variance of Z itself, which also accounts for the variability of V and, for times determined by the observed number of events of an endpoint (trigger), of the analysis time (see lr_cov).

References

Luo X, Mao X, Chen X, Qiu J, Bai S, Quan H (2019). Design and monitoring of survival trials in complex scenarios. Statistics in Medicine 38:192-209.

Schoenfeld D (1981). The asymptotic properties of nonparametric tests for comparing survival distributions. Biometrika 68:316-319.

Yung G, Liu Y (2020). Sample size and power for the weighted log-rank test and Kaplan-Meier based tests with allowance for nonproportional hazards. Biometrics 76:939-950.

See also

lr_cov, ms_events

Examples

ctl <- ms_model(death = log(2) / 12)
trt <- ms_model(death = 0.7 * log(2) / 12)
scn <- ms_scenario(ctl, trt, accrual = ms_accrual(rate = 20))
lr_moments(scn, n = 400, calendar_time = c(24, 36))
#>   time events_control events_treatment   events score_mean     info   z_mean
#> 1   24       105.8727         83.33015 189.2029  -16.77781 47.04842 2.446035
#> 2   36       152.9364        128.18129 281.1176  -24.89193 69.42161 2.987523
#>   z_var
#> 1     1
#> 2     1
